report_name: GitLab Patches Critical CVSS 10.0 Path Traversal Vulnerability

threat_actors.name: Unidentified Scanners
threat_actors.description: Unidentified threat actors observed actively scanning the internet for GitLab instances vulnerable to CVE-2026-85706.

attack_patterns.name: Exploit Public-Facing Application
attack_patterns.description: Threat actors are actively seeking to exploit the path traversal vulnerability CVE-2026-85706 in the GitLab repository commits API to read arbitrary files from vulnerable servers.

attack_patterns.name: Active Scanning
attack_patterns.description: Security researchers observed active in-the-wild probes scanning for GitLab servers vulnerable to the path traversal flaw CVE-2026-85706.

attack_patterns.name: Credentials In Files
attack_patterns.description: A successful exploit of CVE-2026-85706 allows attackers to read arbitrary files, including sensitive data such as application secrets, private source code, and user credentials like those in '/etc/gitlab/gitlab-secrets.json'.

vulnerabilities.name: CVE-2026-85706
vulnerabilities.description: A critical path traversal vulnerability in the GitLab repository commits API allows an unauthenticated, remote attacker to read arbitrary files on a server by sending a specially crafted HTTP request. This could lead to the theft of credentials, source code, and other sensitive data, posing a significant supply chain risk.

vulnerabilities.name: CVE-2026-87719
vulnerabilities.description: A critical insecure deserialization vulnerability in the GitLab GraphQL subscription serializer allows an authenticated user with access to the Duo Chat feature to execute arbitrary code and steal sensitive credentials.

identities.name: GitLab Users
identities.description: Over 100,000 organizations using self-managed GitLab instances are at risk from vulnerabilities CVE-2026-85706 and CVE-2026-87719.

infrastructure.name: Vulnerability Scanning Infrastructure
infrastructure.description: Infrastructure used by unidentified threat actors to actively scan for GitLab servers vulnerable to CVE-2026-85706.

indicators.name: GitLab Path Traversal Attempt (CVE-2026-85706)
indicators.pattern:
title: GitLab Path Traversal Attempt CVE-2026-85706
id: 2b1d3c4e-5f6a-4b9c-8d7e-1a2b3c4d5e6f
status: experimental
description: Detects attempts to exploit the GitLab path traversal vulnerability (CVE-2026-85706) by looking for traversal sequences in requests to the repository commits API endpoint.
references:
  - https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/gitlab-urges-users-to-patch-max-severity-path-traversal-flaw/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-09-11
tags:
  - attack.t1190
  - attack.initial_access
  - cve.2026.85706
level: critical
logsource:
  category: webserver
detection:
  selection_endpoint:
    cs-uri-stem|contains: '/api/v4/projects/'
    cs-uri-stem|endswith: '/repository/commits'
  selection_traversal:
    cs-uri-query|contains:
      - '..%2f'
      - '../'
  condition: all of selection_*
falsepositives:
  - Unlikely, but could be triggered by security scanners.
indicators.description: Detects HTTP requests targeting the GitLab API with path traversal sequences, indicative of exploitation attempts against CVE-2026-85706.

indicators.name: GitLab Secrets File Access
indicators.pattern:
title: GitLab Secrets File Access Attempt
id: 8a7b6c5d-4e3f-4a2b-9c8d-7e6f5a4b3c2d
status: experimental
description: Detects attempts to read the GitLab secrets file, which could occur after successful exploitation of a file read vulnerability like CVE-2026-85706.
references:
  - https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/gitlab-urges-users-to-patch-max-severity-path-traversal-flaw/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-09-11
tags:
  - attack.t1552.001
  - attack.credential_access
level: high
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: linux
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith: '/cat'
    CommandLine|contains: '/etc/gitlab/gitlab-secrets.json'
  condition: selection
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate administrative activity.
indicators.description: Detects command-line execution attempting to read the '/etc/gitlab/gitlab-secrets.json' file, a common post-exploitation step to steal credentials from a compromised GitLab server.
